purpose: Follow each probability-weighted book count into the expected value and the moving balance point.
meaning: The expected value of a finite random variable is the sum of each outcome value multiplied by its probability. It is a probability-weighted mean, can be fractional for integer outcomes, and need not itself be in the support.

definition.setting: An assumed library return-desk model for X, the number of books at one future check-in: X has listed values 0,1,2.

signature.X: Random number of books at the next check-in.
signature.xᵢ: One of the three outcome values 0, 1 or 2 books.
signature.pᵢ: Probability P(X=xᵢ) assigned to outcome xᵢ.
signature.r: Share of the probability left after one-book outcomes, assigned to two books.
signature.E[X]: Expected number of books under this distribution.
signature.xᵢpᵢ: Weighted contribution of outcome xᵢ to the mean.

conditions: The random variable X counts books received at the next library check-in and takes values 0, 1 or 2. These probabilities form an assumed teaching model, not collected library data.
The controls q and r lie between 0 and 1 inclusive. q is the probability of one book; r assigns a share of the remaining probability to two books. The rest goes to zero books.
The probability mass function is p₀=(1−q)(1−r), p₁=q and p₂=(1−q)r. Each mass is nonnegative and their sum is one. A zero mass removes that outcome from the support.
The weighted contribution xᵢpᵢ has units of books; its sum μ=E[X] has the same units. Zero-book probability affects the balance although its weighted value is zero.

A long-run average interpretation requires an appropriate repeated sampling model. Independent repetitions with this fixed finite distribution supply one such setting; expectation itself is defined by the weighted sum.
definition.domain_notes: The primary output is an expected book count in [0,2], not a probability or a promised next result. For this bounded random variable the weighted sum always exists.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources and original finite calculations; independent review pending.

grammar.formation_rule: Use q for the one-book probability. The remaining probability is 1−q; r sends its selected share to two books and 1−r sends the rest to zero books. Thus p₀=(1−q)(1−r), p₁=q and p₂=(1−q)r. Multiply each outcome xᵢ by pᵢ and add: E[X]=0p₀+1p₁+2p₂=q+2(1−q)r books.
grammar.precedence: Construct all three probability masses before weighting their outcome values. Addition combines the weighted contributions, not the unweighted book counts.

prompts.prompt: Can the expected value be 1.25 books?
prompts.answer: Yes. An expectation is a weighted average; a realized return count is still 0, 1 or 2.

prompts.prompt: Can two distributions have the same expectation?
prompts.answer: Yes. A certain one-book count and an equal split between zero and two books both have mean one.
